title: Sandbox writable roots must include the lane's .git/worktrees/<lane>/ dir - index writes currently need elevation
description:
Found by a market-brief-package lane worker on 2026-08-17 (first smoke drain, lane mb-tracker-doc-br-bysf) and routed here at jot-review because the fix is engine sandbox config, not target-repo work. SYMPTOM: from a managed lane worktree, git add on an in-scope file fails with Read-only file system until the same scoped command is elevated. MECHANISM: a linked worktree's index and index.lock live under the MAIN checkout's metadata (<main>/.git/worktrees/<lane>/index.lock), and the sandbox's writable roots cover the lane worktree but not the main checkout's .git/worktrees/<lane>/ directory - so every index write in every managed lane needs elevation, which defeats the sandbox's purpose for the most common git operation a lane performs. OBSERVED PATH: /home/ddc/dev-environment/market-brief-package/.git/worktrees/lane-mb-tracker-doc-br-bysf/index.lock. FIX SHAPE: when constructing a lane sandbox, resolve the worktree's gitdir (cat <worktree>/.git gives 'gitdir: <main>/.git/worktrees/<lane>') and add that directory to the writable roots; nothing else under the main .git should become writable. TEST SPEC: an integration test that creates a managed lane worktree, runs git add on a tracked file inside the sandbox profile, and asserts success without elevation; negative control asserts the main checkout's .git objects/refs remain read-only.

## Acceptance Criteria

A managed lane can git add/commit in its worktree without elevation; the main checkout's .git remains read-only outside .git/worktrees/<lane>/; regression test pins both.

title: Codex first-run hooks-trust modal blocks dispatched lanes
description: Reproduced live 2026-08-13, first dispatch of abacus run (see ab-geh notes). A codex agent started by herdr agent start --kind codex in a fresh worktree lane (~/.herdr/worktrees/abacus/lane-ab-v8s) presents an interactive review modal on startup: 3 hooks need review before they can run, Press t to trust all (2 PreToolUse, 1 SessionStart — the operator's own kept hooks from ~/.codex config). The dispatched prompt is never processed; the lane does zero work. Repro: herdr worktree create on this repo, herdr agent start x --kind codex --pane <pane>, herdr agent read x — the modal is on screen. Investigation directions, evidence-gated per MVP-first: find where codex stores hook trust (global vs per-directory — if per-directory, every fresh worktree will hit this) and whether a config flag or codex exec style non-interactive invocation bypasses the modal for already-operator-approved hooks. The fix belongs in how abacus (or herdr agent start) launches codex, not in removing the hooks.
acceptance_criteria: A freshly created worktree lane started with herdr agent start --kind codex reaches the composer with hooks active and processes its dispatch prompt without any interactive keypress. Verified by dispatching a trivial bead through abacus run end to end with no manual send-keys.
notes: RESOLVED BY EVIDENCE, 2026-08-13 evening. Probe: fresh worktree lane (w1R, branch lane/probe-5pe), herdr agent start --kind codex — codex v0.147.0 reached its composer directly, no modal. Mechanism found: codex stores hook trust in ~/.codex/config.toml under [hooks.state], one entry per hook keyed by source path + event + index, holding a sha256 trusted_hash of the hook content. Scope is GLOBAL and content-addressed, not per-directory: the single manual trust-all during run 1 of ab-geh covered all future lanes. The run-1 modal was the one-time first-run review of the operator's kept hooks after the SABLE hook removal reshuffled configs. Recurrence condition: any hook content change or new hook re-triggers one global review modal, and a lane dispatched in that window stalls exactly like run 1 — detection of that is ab-zkq's outcome probe, which is the correct layer; no launch-path change in abacus is warranted. Acceptance verified live: dispatch 2 (lane w1S, bead ab-zkq) went end to end with no manual keypress — prompt received and worker running. Probe lane fully torn down.
close_reason: No engine change warranted: hook trust is global and content-addressed in ~/.codex/config.toml [hooks.state]; the one-time operator trust covers all lanes. Recurrence (hook content change) stalls a lane detectably — that detection is ab-zkq scope.

title: Herdr workspaces vanish without a remove call — prior-invocation warm lanes lost (reproduced; reap exonerated)
description:
## Summary

`abacus reap` appears to sweep herdr workspaces it did not create. During the 2026-08-18 mb-dss7 campaign the parked `market-brief-package-workers` workspace vanished twice, each time in the exact window where an abacus-dispatched lane settled and reaped: w33 was lost during the w36 (mb-dss7.4) reap, w37 during the w38 (mb-dss7.5) reap. `herdr tab create` then returned `workspace_not_found`; `herdr agent list` showed only current-cycle agents surviving.

Each sweep killed parked warm workers and re-paid the orientation tax the warm-author standard (ab-co5 ruling) exists to avoid — hence P1.

Hypothesis: reap matches victims by cwd prefix (all these workspaces share the market-brief-package checkout path) rather than by identity of the resources it created at dispatch.

One earlier single-tab disappearance predates any reap and is NOT explained by this hypothesis — keep it out of scope here.

## Steps to Reproduce

Create two herdr workspaces whose cwds share a path prefix. Dispatch an abacus lane into one, let it settle, run reap. Observe whether the foreign workspace is destroyed.

## Suggested approach

At dispatch, record the exact identities (workspace/tab/agent ids) of every resource abacus creates; reap sweeps only recorded identities. Never select victims by cwd prefix or name pattern.

## Test spec

Red-first in the abacus test suite: (1) reap with a created-resource registry leaves a foreign workspace sharing the cwd prefix untouched — this must FAIL against current behavior if the hypothesis is right; (2) positive control: reap does sweep the workspace it created (guards against a vacuous pass where reap sweeps nothing).

## Acceptance Criteria

The two-workspace repro leaves the foreign workspace alive while the lane workspace is reaped; abacus suite green.
notes: Diagnosis 2026-08-19 on Herdr 0.8.0: the stated two-workspace reproduction does not reproduce. Current src/main.rs dispatch_cycle lines 856-943 records workspace.workspace_id from the worktree create JSON and passes only that exact ID to both normal and forced worktree removal; git blame shows this behavior has existed since commit 8de776a on 2026-08-14, before the reported 2026-08-18 losses. Real-substrate probe used a disposable git repo plus foreign workspace w3D and owned worktree workspaces w3E and w3F sharing repo_key and path prefix. Removing w3E with herdr worktree remove --workspace w3E removed w3E and workspace get w3D still succeeded. A dirty index in w3F produced dirty_worktree_requires_force; removing w3F with the same exact ID plus --force removed w3F and workspace get w3D still succeeded. Live worktree create JSON matched parse_worktree_created field paths. All disposable workspaces and files were cleaned up. Existing integration test tests/br_roundtrip.rs::abacus_run_reaps_a_clean_lane_without_force_after_the_worker_closes_its_bead already asserts the exact-ID command. No source fix or red-first regression is supportable from current evidence. To resume, provide a captured command transcript or Herdr event/server log from one loss, or a new reproduction that fails on Herdr 0.8.0; likely next suspects are the interim manual worker-workspace practice or another actor, not Abacus cwd-prefix selection.

title: br ready --json omits labels required by dispatch filtering
description:
Blocking discovery while implementing ab-hmw. In the pinned br binary, br ready --json omits the labels field even for an open ready bead labeled seat:operator, while br show <id> --json and br label list expose the label. This invalidates ab-hmw's stated assumption that ReadyBead can deserialize labels directly from ready output and would silently dispatch operator-seat work. The engine now mitigates this with a second filtered ready query, but the substrate serialization defect remains. Relevant engine functions are ReadyBead, parse_ready, and select_bead in src/lib.rs and cmd_run in src/main.rs. Suggested resolution: fix br ready JSON upstream to serialize labels and pin that version; remove the engine's extra membership query only after the fixed live contract is verified.

## File footprint

src/lib.rs, src/main.rs, tests/br_roundtrip.rs, plus the upstream br ready JSON serializer or dependency pin once located.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a fresh temporary tracker with br init --prefix it.
2. Create an open priority-0 bead and add seat:operator with br label add.
3. Run br ready --json and observe no labels key.
4. Run br show <id> --json and observe labels containing seat:operator.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The pinned br ready --json output includes labels for labeled ready beads and an empty or default representation for unlabeled beads.
- An upstream integration test locks that serializer contract.
- The real temp-workspace test in tests/br_roundtrip.rs remains green.
- Only then may cmd_run's filtered second ready query be removed, with unit and integration tests updated before implementation.
- Full suite, cargo clippy, and cargo fmt --check green.
notes: ab-hmw mitigates the omission in the engine by intersecting primary ready output with br ready --label seat:operator --json before selection. The substrate serialization defect remains open; removing the extra query requires a pinned br version whose ready JSON includes labels.
close_reason: Resolved by the substrate upgrade: br 0.3.2 emits the labels field in ready --json, verified on the live store (ab-72p itself listed with seat:operator). The engine's membership-query workaround is now removable — tracked as the unblocked follow-up bead.

title: CI groundwork: standard workflow, rust-version pin, br skip guards, shim BR_REAL

title: Engine recognizes contract-BLOCKED lanes: drain parks them and continues instead of aborting
description:
The engine cannot distinguish a contract-compliant BLOCKED worker from a stalled one, and a drain aborts entirely on the first such lane. probe_bead_outcome (src/main.rs:708) classifies only Completed / Incomplete / NeverEngaged from bead status. A worker that executes the AGENTS.md BLOCKED protocol correctly — appends a "BLOCKED: ..." comment to its bead, files the blocker bead with a dep link, leaves the worktree uncommitted, stops without closing — reads as Incomplete: cmd_run exits 1 with "worker engaged but the run is incomplete", and cmd_drain (src/main.rs:743) propagates the same Err through dispatch_cycle(...)? and ABORTS the whole loop. Under the north-star success condition (N ready beads drain overnight, zero interventions) one legitimately blocked lane must not end the night: it should park and the drain should continue with the next ready bead.

Observed 2026-08-17, first foreign-repo smoke chain (market-brief): two consecutive lanes executed the BLOCKED protocol perfectly (mb-tracker-doc-br-bysf blocked by mb-8ftb; mb-8ftb blocked first by mb-rh6c then mb-p8px) and each read as a generic failure requiring the orchestrator to read the pane, diagnose, and hand-drive resume. Evidence trail: abacus epic ab-mbp-onboard-hb0.6 comments.

Scope (deliberately narrow):
1. Detect BLOCKED in the outcome probe. Signal: the bead is in_progress AND its most recent comment begins with "BLOCKED" (the contract mandates that durable comment before stopping; the comment is already the source of truth). Add BeadOutcome::Blocked.
2. cmd_run: exit non-zero still, but with a distinct "lane blocked: <first line of the BLOCKED comment>" report, and DO reap the lane worktree only if clean — a blocked lane may hold uncommitted work; if dirty, leave it and say so.
3. cmd_drain: a Blocked outcome does not abort the loop — record the bead id in a blocked set (like lost_claims), print the same distinct report, and continue selecting other ready beads. Drain exit summarizes blocked lanes at the end.

title: Reap tries clean removal first; force only as loud fallback
description:
src/main.rs line 206 area: the reap path passes --force to herdr worktree remove unconditionally for completed lanes. description:
Story: S5 + S6 (ADR 0005 D1 second half, D2, D6). The wedge: LaneState derivation, sweep-then-dispatch drain, morning report, exit codes.

What: (1) LaneState enum {Authoring, Blocked, AwaitingReview, ReworkRequested, Merged, Stalled} derived statelessly per cycle from three probes: br show (BeadOutcome from C2), herdr agent list (deterministic names via sanitize_agent_name), gh pr view --json state,mergedAt on branch lane/<bead-id>. Truth table per ADR D1 incl. cycle bookkeeping hooks (this bead lands the derivation with review-related inputs stubbed as parameters — verdict-heading count, latest adjudication + adjudicated head — so C4/C5 plug in without re-deriving; until then those inputs are None and AwaitingReview simply means bead closed + PR open). An accepted adjudication with unmerged PR stays AwaitingReview. (2) cmd_drain becomes sweep-then-dispatch: sweep re-derives live lanes and acts (this bead: park Blocked with reap-only-if-clean via the inverted is_dirty_worktree_remove_error path — NO --force for Blocked; report Stalled; reap Merged; review/rework actions arrive in C4/C5/C6 behind the stubbed inputs), then dispatches at most one ready bead. Drain NEVER aborts on Blocked/AwaitingReview/Stalled; exits 0 when no ready beads remain and no transition pending, printing the per-class morning report (one line per class with bead ids and format_lane_duration; empty classes omitted). (3) Exit codes per ratified D6: drain 0 on clean loop regardless of mix; run 0 = nominal settle (Completed/Merged or AwaitingReview), 3 = Blocked/Stalled, 1 = engine failure. Lane-state layer owns the code.

Gotchas: probe only lanes whose state can change (Blocked and Merged are absorbing until human action) to bound gh calls. The existing outcome match (Incomplete/NeverEngaged → Err) is REPLACED for drain — Stalled records and continues; keep NeverEngaged's one re-prompt retry as-is before classifying Stalled. gh pr view on a branch with no PR must classify as no-PR, not error (see land.rs candidate handling).

Unit tests: lane_state_derivation_truth_table (~2 fns in src/lane.rs tests) with the concrete probe triples from TEST-STRATEGY incl. the negative (AwaitingReview derives from comment absence, never from combined-status "pending"); morning_report_renders_every_settle_class_with_bead_ids.

Integration — fake-shim in tests/drain.rs (reuse TempDir + make_executable harness): (1) drain_records_a_blocked_settle_and_continues_to_the_next_bead — 2 ready beads, worker 1 flips fake-br to in_progress + BLOCKED comment, worker 2 closes; expect exit 0 (THIS IS RED against pre-cluster HEAD — the wedge's red-first proof), both lanes opened, blocked lane NOT reaped, report contains blocked: 1 and completed: 1. (2) drain_records_awaiting_review_and_exits_when_nothing_is_actionable — lane settles closed with open fake PR, no adjudication ever; expect exit 0, report awaiting-review: 1. (3) a_dirty_blocked_lane_is_left_standing_and_reported — fake herdr non-forced remove returns the captured dirty error; expect removal calls exactly [non-forced], NO --force, exit 0 (deliberate inversion of abacus_run_warns_and_forces_removal_when_a_completed_lane_is_dirty, which must survive verbatim — distinct behaviors, never folded).

Integration — real-br in tests/br_roundtrip.rs (the ONLY two real-br additions this cluster permits): (4) abacus_drain_classifies_a_real_blocked_comment_and_continues — fake-herdr prompt step runs real br comments add "$bead" "BLOCKED: fixture reason", second bead closes; exit 0, blocked bead still in_progress with comment intact. (5) abacus_run_classifies_a_superseded_blocked_comment_as_stalled — real br add BLOCKED then "resuming"; expect run classifies stalled (exit 3 per D6).

Verification: cargo test, cargo clippy, cargo fmt --check. Requires C1 (module seams) and C2 (Blocked outcome).

title: Lifecycle: review module — grammar constants, refutation brief, ephemeral reviewer launch
description:
Story: S1 (ADR 0005 D3, D8). The review module: grammar constants, refutation-brief generation, ephemeral reviewer launch.

What: new src/review.rs owning EVERY textual grammar (D8): the BLOCKED token constant (moved from its C2 interim home), the verdict-comment heading grammar ("## Adversarial review — cycle <n>" and the re-review variant), the adjudication grammar constants (heading, verdict lines, per-finding disposition forms, "Adjudicated head:" line — parsing itself is C5), the status context string "adversarial-review", and the brief template. Brief builder: from bead id + description + comments (authority trail) + PR number + target repo AGENTS.md path, produce the refutation brief — authority map, per-bead refutation targets, read-only ground rules with EXACTLY one permitted write (gh pr comment on the target PR), required verdict grammar REFUTED / NOT REFUTED with numbered findings and a Probes section. Brief written to the gitignored tmp path in the target repo (deterministic path containing the bead id). Reviewer launch modeled on dispatch_resolution (src/main.rs:310–354) with one deliberate difference: dispatch_resolution uses herdr worktree open, while THIS launch uses herdr workspace create --cwd <target main checkout> --no-focus (D3: reviewers get a dedicated workspace on the main checkout, never a worktree). Then agent start --kind codex under a DETERMINISTIC per-bead-per-cycle name (e.g. rev-<sanitized-bead>-c<n>; the liveness signal C3's bookkeeping reads), prompt BY FILE PATH, monitored with prompt --wait plus the existing stall retry. Never headless, never split off an orchestrator pane; reviewer pane disposable after its verdict posts (removal wiring in C5's sweep actions).

Gotchas: LAUNCHING.md (at /home/ddc/dev-environment/bb-skills/agents/LAUNCHING.md — outside this repo) has a measured-broken step 4 (agent wait --until idle never fires for codex agents) — never use it; prompt --wait is the verified form (ADR 0005 Context). Fresh codex may stop at a hook-trust dialog — that is an operator matter; the engine treats a reviewer that never posts as an unadjudicated-absent verdict (lane simply stays AwaitingReview; no retry storm). The one-write rule is enforced by brief text, not machinery.

Unit tests (src/review.rs test module, modeled on dispatch_prompt_carries_bead_identity_and_protocol): (1) refutation_brief_carries_targets_ground_rules_and_verdict_grammar — brief contains bead id, PR number, gh pr comment as sole permitted write, verdict grammar, Probes requirement, authority map; NEGATIVE: brief must NOT contain git push, br close, or br update instructions. (2) brief_path_is_inside_the_repo_gitignored_tmp_dir — deterministic path builder. (3) reviewer name builder: deterministic, herdr-grammar-safe (reuse sanitize_agent_name rules), distinct across cycles.

Integration — fake-shim in tests/drain.rs: sweep_launches_one_ephemeral_reviewer_for_a_newly_awaiting_review_lane — herdr log shows exactly one dedicated workspace create (NOT the lane's workspace), one agent start --kind codex, one agent prompt <reviewer> <existing-file-path> --wait; across TWO sweep iterations exactly one launch; grep-negative over the whole herdr log: no "agent wait --until idle" anywhere.

Verification: cargo test, cargo clippy, cargo fmt --check. Requires C3 (AwaitingReview state and sweep action seams).

title: Lifecycle: adjudication parsing and the commit-status lifecycle
description:
Story: S2 + S3 (ADR 0005 D4, D8; S3 per the RESEARCH-gate ruling: advisory status, enforcement is onboarding-owned). Adjudication parsing and the commit-status lifecycle.

What: in src/review.rs (shared grammar seam with C4): (1) adjudication parser — recognizes ONLY PR comments with the adjudication heading (## Adjudication — cycle <k>); extracts overall verdict (accepted | rework), per-finding dispositions (accepted / rejected / rerouted with destinations), and the Adjudicated head SHA line. Reviewer verdict comments are recognized BY HEADING ONLY for existence/cycle counting — their bodies are never parsed (an unadjudicated REFUTED must flip nothing). Latest adjudication cycle wins. (2) adjudication body BUILDER for the engine-posted cases, round-tripping through the parser. (3) Commit-status helpers via the statuses API only (POST repos/{o}/{r}/statuses/{sha}, context exactly adversarial-review): a two-variant state enum Pending/Success — failure is UNREPRESENTABLE at the type level; combined-status reader distinguishing absent (zero statuses ALSO reads state pending on the combined endpoint) from posted-pending. (4) Sweep wiring in src/lane.rs: post pending exactly once when a lane first reaches AwaitingReview; flip to success only on an accepting adjudication; rework adjudications post NOTHING new; reap the ephemeral reviewer workspace after its verdict comment exists. Plug the C3 stubs: verdict-heading count, latest adjudication + adjudicated head feed the LaneState derivation (ReworkRequested = latest adjudication is rework AND branch head == adjudicated head).

Fixtures: captured verbatim from the PR 25/26 production records (gh pr view --comments on DDC-Heartwood/market-intelligence, inline as consts per the WORKTREE_CREATED_FIXTURE precedent) plus live gh api combined-status output. Note: records posted before 2026-08-18 late-day carry SHAs in prose, not the fixed Adjudicated head line — the parser handles the FIXED grammar only; fixture selection uses post-adoption shapes or hand-adjusted captures marked as such.

Unit tests (src/review.rs): parses_the_captured_accepted_adjudication; parses_a_rework_requesting_adjudication; reviewer_verdict_bodies_are_never_parsed_as_adjudications (captured cycle-1 REFUTED verdict → NotAdjudication); latest_adjudication_cycle_wins; adjudication_body_builder_round_trips_through_the_parser (builder→parser equality on parsed values — the D8 drift tripwire, highest-leverage test in the cluster); status_context_and_states_are_pending_or_success_only (path, context, full rendering set == {"pending","success"}); combined_status_reader_distinguishes_absent_from_posted_pending.

Integration — fake-shim in tests/drain.rs (budget 2 fns if the state machine gets hairy): sweep_posts_pending_once_then_flips_success_only_after_an_accepting_adjudication — phase 1: AwaitingReview → exactly one statuses POST state pending; phase 2: rework adjudication appears → NO new POST; phase 3: accepted adjudication → one success POST. Grep-negatives over the whole fake-gh log: no "failure" state ever; no ruleset or branch-protection mutation calls (tests/land.rs assert_no_forbidden_flags style — the engine never writes enforcement config).

Verification: cargo test, cargo clippy, cargo fmt --check. Requires C4 (grammar constants, reviewer names).

title: Lifecycle: warm lanes — reap on merge, rework into the same agent, same-branch recovery
description:
Story: S4 (ADR 0005 D5). Warm lanes: reap on merge, rework into the same agent, recovery on the same branch.

What: (1) Reap policy by LaneState in src/lane.rs: Merged → reap (force allowed, as today); Blocked → only when clean (landed in C3); AwaitingReview / ReworkRequested / Stalled → never automatically. The lane workspace and agent stay alive from settle through merge or operator abandon. (2) Rework redispatch: on ReworkRequested (from C5's derivation), prompt the EXISTING agent (name re-derived via sanitize_agent_name(bead_id)) with a rework spec generated from the adjudication comment — accepted findings with destinations, the adjudicated head, and the branch lane/<bead-id>; the PR updates in place. Rework outranks fresh dispatch within a sweep iteration (D2). The bead is reopened by the adjudicating side — the engine never reopens beads. (3) Recovery: if the warm agent is absent from herdr agent list, recreate the lane on the SAME lane/<bead-id> branch. LIVE-TOOL VERIFICATION REQUIRED in this bead (manual, before implementing the fallback): herdr worktree create behavior when the branch already exists — if it errors or mints a new branch, fall back to git worktree add on the existing branch + herdr workspace create --cwd that path + agent start. Record the observed behavior in this bead's notes.

Gotchas: sanitize_agent_name truncates to 32 chars and maps every char outside [a-z0-9-_] — uppercase included — to '-', forcing a leading a-z (it does NOT case-fold), so distinct ids can alias harder than case-folding would suggest (e.g. AB-1 and CD-1 both sanitize to a--1); not constructible with realistic bead ids, no test, but note the class in code where the name is derived. Merged detection: reuse parse_queue_state/observe_queue_state or the lighter gh pr view --json state,mergedAt (RESEARCH: both suffice; pick one and say why in the PR).

title: Transient probe failure aborts the run before the never-engaged retry can fire
description:
Observed 2026-08-14 18:13, first dispatch on the upgraded substrate:
the lane settled instantly (lost-prompt race, third occurrence — the
ab-f5f retry is merged and live) but the outcome probe itself failed —
br show <bead> --json exited 7 with empty stderr, aborting abacus run
before the probe could classify NeverEngaged, so the f5f retry never
ran. The same command succeeded manually seconds later: a transient of
the known database-busy-during-index-setup class (jotted 2026-08-14 on
0.1.45, now observed on 0.3.2), plausibly the store's first index pass
after the JSONL rebuild. Composition gap: any transient br error at
probe time masks the retry machinery entirely.

Fix in cmd_run (src/main.rs): when the post-settle br show probe exits
non-zero, retry the probe once after a short delay (about two seconds)
before propagating the error; only a second consecutive failure aborts
the run. This composes with the existing NeverEngaged retry — a probe
that succeeds on its second attempt feeds the normal classification,
which can then trigger the f5f re-prompt as designed.

## File footprint

src/main.rs, tests/br_roundtrip.rs

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Dispatch a bead while the shared store is briefly busy (first access
   after a JSONL rebuild reproduces the window).
2. The settle returns, the probe's br show exits non-zero transiently,
   and abacus run exits 1 without classifying or retrying anything.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Unit test covers the probe-retry decision: first non-zero probe
  triggers exactly one delayed re-probe; a second failure propagates
  the original error shape.
- A probe that succeeds on retry feeds normal outcome classification,
  including the NeverEngaged re-prompt path.
- Full suite, clippy, fmt green within budget.

title: Dispatch race: prompt pastes into the codex composer but never submits; engine misreads its own claim as worker engagement
description: Observed 2026-08-19 ~17:08 on the go4.2 dispatch (lane w3N, first dispatch on the binary built from fe186e7, codex v0.148.0). SIGNATURE: herdr agent prompt <name> <prompt> --wait returned a successful agent_prompted response, but the codex TUI held the entire dispatch prompt in its composer as unsubmitted pasted content (pane read showed a Pasted Content 1004 chars input line, Context 0% used); the agent settled to done without processing anything; the abacus outcome probe then printed: bead ab-lifecycle-v2-go4.2 is in_progress; worker engaged but the run is incomplete after 9s — and exited 1. Two distinct defects. HERDR-SIDE RACE: the prompt submission reported success while the TUI had consumed the paste but not the submit keypress — likely a startup race, since the pane banner had just rendered; this is a different signature from the captured-agent-prompt-stall error that src/lane.rs already retries once (that path fired and recovered on the ab-m1r dispatch the same day; this one returns success so no retry triggers). ENGINE-SIDE MISCLASSIFICATION: the probe asserts worker engaged from the bead being in_progress, but the ENGINE claims the bead itself before opening the lane, so in_progress carries zero information about the worker; a truthful engagement signal exists (the worker posts nothing, the agent context stays at 0 percent, the composer still holds the paste). This is input evidence for ab-lifecycle-v2-go4.3's LaneState derivation — engagement must be derived from worker-observable effects, not from state the engine wrote itself. RECOVERY PROCEDURE (validated live): herdr agent send-keys <agent> Enter submits the pending composer content; the worker then proceeds normally — confirm via herdr pane read <pane> --source recent-unwrapped that the state line shows Working and context usage rises. SUGGESTED FIX SHAPE: after a successful prompt, verify engagement by an observable (agent transitions to working, or a bounded re-check that the composer is empty) before concluding the settle probe; on paste-without-submit, one send-keys Enter nudge then re-wait. Whether the underlying submit race is fixable herdr-side should be raised with herdr — record findings here either way. title: Default-branch discovery fails on checkouts without refs/remotes/origin/HEAD, blocking every dispatch
description:
Observed 2026-08-15 ~13:55 UTC, first dispatch after installing the PR-21/PR-23 binary: abacus run exited 1 before selection with: abacus run: git symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD failed (exit status: 128): fatal: ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD is not a symbolic ref.

Cause: the D14 default-branch discovery (added in PR 21, discovery call site in cmd_run, src/main.rs) assumes refs/remotes/origin/HEAD exists. That ref is created by git clone only — a checkout built with git init + git remote add never has it, and a checkout can also lose or carry a stale one across a remote URL change (this checkout's origin was re-pointed to the org repository the same day). The failure precedes selection, so it blocks EVERY dispatch on an affected checkout — run, and by construction drain.

Workaround applied to the operator checkout, which resolves the immediate block: git remote set-head origin -a (sets origin/HEAD from the remote's advertised HEAD). Any other affected checkout needs the same until fixed.

Fix in the discovery call site (keep discovery out of the pure prompt function per D14): when git symbolic-ref exits non-zero, fall back to resolving the remote's advertised default — git ls-remote --symref origin HEAD (parse the "ref: refs/heads/<name> HEAD" line) — and optionally repair the local ref with git remote set-head origin -a for subsequent runs. Only if both paths fail should the dispatch abort, with an error naming both attempts.

## File footprint

src/main.rs, tests/br_roundtrip.rs

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In a scratch repo: git init, add a commit, git remote add origin <any real remote>, git fetch origin (note: no origin/HEAD is created).
2. Run abacus run against it (or observe the operator-checkout instance above).
3. The run exits 1 at discovery, before selection, with the symbolic-ref 128 error.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Unit or integration test covers the discovery fallback: a fixture checkout WITHOUT refs/remotes/origin/HEAD still resolves the default branch (extend the PR-21 real-git fixture pattern in tests/br_roundtrip.rs; the existing origin/HEAD-present case must keep passing).
- A checkout with neither resolvable path produces a single clear error naming both attempted mechanisms.
- Full suite, clippy -D warnings, fmt --check green.

title: Adversarial PR review gate: build the pane-review step into the abacus lane flow globally
description: Requested by the operator 2026-08-18 from the market-brief-package cockpit after the flow proved out manually. EVIDENCE: first production use 2026-08-18 in market-brief-package — both wave-1 PRs (25, 26) returned REFUTED with real blockers (unbounded year window enabling memory exhaustion on the model-facing path; a test mock wider than the real collector seam; refusal turns able to mutate a working set the ADR requires unchanged; shallow payload validation persisting machine-dependent paths into an append-only log). description: Currently the worker protocol in dispatch_prompt (src/lib.rs) ends at push plus br close, and the orchestrator opens PRs by hand — PRs 1 through 4 were all manual gh pr create calls. title: abacus run cannot tell a gated lane from a finished one
description: Reproduced live 2026-08-13, first dispatch (see ab-geh notes). herdr agent prompt --wait settled with agent_status done while the codex worker was actually parked on a startup modal and had processed nothing: no claim on the bead, no commit, no push. abacus run printed the settle JSON and exited 0 — a false success. The settle state alone is not evidence of work. Cheapest evidence-based check per MVP-first, in src/main.rs cmd_run after settle: shell br show <bead-id> --json in the lane checkout (the Lane struct already carries checkout_path) and report the bead status the worker left behind — closed means done, in_progress means it worked but did not finish, still open means the worker never engaged (exit non-zero and say so). Do not build state-machine heuristics over herdr agent states; one br probe distinguishes the three outcomes that matter. Test spec: unit test the outcome classification from bead status; integration test the open-bead path with a fake lane dir holding an initialized br workspace. Needs ab-5pe understood first only if the fix shape ends up in the launch path; the report-what-the-bead-says probe stands alone.
acceptance_criteria: After settle, abacus run probes br show <bead-id> --json in the lane checkout and reports the outcome from bead status: closed exits 0 as success, in_progress reports incomplete, open reports never-engaged, both non-zero. Unit test covers the three-way classification; integration test covers the open path with a real br workspace in a temp lane dir. Run-1 conditions (worker gated on a modal, settle says done) would exit non-zero.
notes: Corroboration, 2026-08-13: the abacus-v1 orchestrator hit the identical failure independently the same night (herdr done treated as completion while the agent was parked), and the sf reference implementation states the rule outright: either signal is a doorbell, not evidence. Three independent arrivals — this run, v1's, and sf's — make the failure structural, not incidental. The fix shape stands: probe br in the lane for the bead status; never treat runtime agent state as an outcome.

title: Dispatch prompt orders close after push, stranding bead state in the lane
description: Observed on the first successful lane (run 2 of ab-geh, 2026-08-13). dispatch_prompt in src/lib.rs instructs the worker: commit, push with git push -u origin <branch>, then br close <id>. The close therefore mutates the lane's .beads/issues.jsonl AFTER the branch is pushed, leaving the closed status as an uncommitted working-tree change in the worktree — the pushed branch carries the bead as open, and the main checkout's tracker learns nothing. The codex worker on lane/ab-v8s reported exactly this: only uncommitted change is .beads/issues.jsonl, produced by the requested post-push br close. Fix shape: reorder the protocol in dispatch_prompt to close the bead before the final commit+push so the branch carries its own completion record (br close, then git add .beads, commit, push). Update the dispatch_prompt unit test in src/lib.rs to assert the ordering (close appears before push in the prompt text). Note the residual gap is claim/close visibility across live lanes generally — that is the known no-tree-claim-coordination hazard, out of scope here; this bead only stops the protocol from stranding state by construction.
acceptance_criteria: dispatch_prompt orders the protocol as br close, then commit including .beads, then push — the pushed lane branch carries the bead closed status. The dispatch_prompt unit test asserts close appears before push in the prompt text. A dispatched lane leaves no uncommitted .beads changes after settling.
notes: Run-3 evidence (zkq lane): the codex worker improvised the correct behavior unprompted — after the instructed push it closed the bead, committed the jsonl as a second commit (7672d49 tracker: close ab-zkq), and pushed again, so the branch carried its close and the lane reaped with no force. The bead remains valid: the protocol should make this deterministic in dispatch_prompt rather than worker-dependent improvisation. Also note the reap contrast: v8s lane (no close commit) required forced removal; zkq lane (close committed) removed clean.
